package.welcome_message: Welcome to a 3-day Jordan adventure: Amman and Wadi Rum, curated with authentic Jordanian experiences and local hosts.

trip.title: Amman & Wadi Rum Cultural Journey
trip.summary: Three days exploring the heart of Jordan: a relaxed evening in Amman followed by two immersive days in the iconic desert of Wadi Rum. Each day is focused on one region, with outdoor visits in the morning and cultural or culinary experiences in the afternoon and evening.

planning.strategy: Each day stays in one area: Amman, then Wadi Rum (2 days). Walk heritage and nature in the morning. Save museums, meals, and shade for the afternoon. About 3 places to visit and 2 meals each day.
assumptions: Travel times between cities are estimated qualitatively, not as exact minutes, unless evidence exists.
Opening hours are used only when present on the catalog record.

climate.typical_pattern: High daytime heat, especially in the Jordan Valley and desert.
climate.outdoor_guidance: Walk outdoors in the morning. Keep the afternoon for shade, meals, or indoor visits.

decisions.title: Each day stays in one area
decisions.why: Mixing far-apart cities in one day makes the trip exhausting and confusing.
decisions.effect: Your days follow Amman, then Wadi Rum (2 days).

decisions.title: This trip stays in one part of Jordan
decisions.why: 3 days is too short for both the north and the south.
decisions.effect: So this journey focuses on the south, and those places get proper time.

decisions.title: Your first night is near the airport
decisions.effect: Night one is a hotel in Amman, as close to the airport as the listings allow.

decisions.title: Settle in this evening
decisions.effect: Dinner near the hotel, then rest. No sightseeing after a late-day flight.

decisions.title: Then you move closer to the places you came for
decisions.why: Sleeping in the same city you visit beats a long commute every morning.
decisions.effect: After the arrival night, nearby days share one hotel. You only move when the next area is too far for a day trip.

decisions.title: Your must-see places get proper time
decisions.why: Wadi Rum were marked as required.
decisions.effect: Those places are planned from real sites in that area, not borrowed from a nearby city.

days.summary: Evening arrival in Amman: eat if you can, then sleep. Visiting starts tomorrow.

schedule.name: Cantaloupe Gastro Pub
schedule.description: A sophisticated rooftop gastro pub in Jabal Amman offering stunning citadel views, gourmet bites, and craft cocktails.
schedule.reason: Dinner near the hotel. Nothing more tonight.
matched_preferences: One visit covering the nearby monuments

schedule.name: InterContinental Jordan
schedule.description: Long-established five-star IHG hotel on Islamic College Street in Jabal Amman, between the Second and Third Circles, with six restaurants, indoor and outdoor pools, a spa and a 24-hour reception.
schedule.reason: Check in and sleep. Sightseeing starts tomorrow. 5-star stay, as requested

days.transport_notes: You land at 19:45. The drive from Queen Alia to Amman is about 45 minutes. Times below start after that transfer.

days.summary: Morning exploration of the desert's iconic dunes and villages, followed by a local Bedouin lunch and an evening desert camp dinner.

schedule.name: Red Sand Dunes of Wadi Rum
schedule.description: Striking high red sand dunes leaning against sandstone mountain cliffs in central Wadi Rum.
schedule.reason: Iconic Wadi Rum landscape, a must-visit for any desert experience.

schedule.name: Rum Village Bedouin Oasis
schedule.description: The main Bedouin residential village and hub for desert tour departures inside Wadi Rum.
schedule.reason: Cultural insight into Bedouin life and a gateway for further desert adventures.
matched_preferences: One visit covering the nearby monuments

schedule.name: Barrah Canyon
schedule.description: A 5-kilometer long majestic sandstone canyon in eastern Wadi Rum favored for desert trekking and rock climbing.
schedule.reason: Scenic trekking route offering panoramic desert views and a quieter side of Wadi Rum.

schedule.name: Wadi Rum Rest House Restaurant
schedule.description: Historic entrance hub eatery in Wadi Rum Village offering simple local meals and drinks.
schedule.reason: Authentic Bedouin cuisine in a convenient location after the morning hikes.
matched_preferences: One visit covering the nearby monuments

schedule.name: Rahayeb Desert Camp Restaurant
schedule.description: Bedouin camp dining area set against sandstone cliffs in protected Wadi Rum valley.
schedule.reason: Evening desert dining experience with traditional Bedouin fare and starlit ambience.

days.transport_notes: This evening you check in to your hotel in Wadi Rum.

days.summary: Morning visits to historic forts and petroglyph sites, followed by a Bedouin lunch and a final desert camp dinner.

schedule.name: Desert Police Station & Fort (Wadi Rum)
schedule.description: An active stone desert patrol fort in Rum Village staffed by traditional Jordan Desert Patrol officers.
schedule.reason: Cultural insight into Jordan's desert patrol heritage.
matched_preferences: A second day to go beyond the main site
One visit covering the nearby monuments

schedule.name: Khazali Canyon
schedule.description: A narrow fissure canyon in Jebel Khazali famous for ancient Thamudic, Anati, and Nabataean petroglyphs.
schedule.reason: Historic rock art site offering a quiet, reflective experience.

schedule.name: Lawrence's Spring
schedule.description: A natural mountain spring nestled in Wadi Rum, associated with T.E. Lawrence's desert travels.
schedule.reason: Historical landmark with a tranquil setting, perfect for a reflective pause.

schedule.name: Rum Magic Restaurant
schedule.description: Authentic Bedouin dining experience serving traditional Zarb (underground slow-cooked meat and rice) near Wadi Rum entrance.
schedule.reason: Culinary highlight of the desert, offering a hearty Bedouin meal in a unique setting.
matched_preferences: One visit covering the nearby monuments

schedule.name: Bedouin Night Camp Restaurant
schedule.description: Secluded desert camp dining space in Wadi Rum serving authentic Bedouin meals.
schedule.reason: Nighttime desert dining with traditional music and stargazing, completing the cultural immersion.
